# components/scrollspy

<!-- GENERATED by scripts/build-docs.ts from components/scrollspy/scrollspy.ts — edit the source, then `deno task docs`. -->

Import: `import { ScrollSpy } from "@tundralibs/ui/scrollspy"`

Shown on its demo page (`deno task build:demos`, then `demo/components/scrollspy.html`). Guides: [Getting started](../UI-Getting-Started.md) · [rAPId integration](../UI-Rapid.md) · [Theming](../UI-Theming.md).

## Functions

### `ScrollSpy`

```ts
ScrollSpy(props: ScrollSpyProps): Html
```

"On this page" links that follow the reader: scrollspy.js marks the link
of the section nearest the top (`aria-current="true"`, `.is-active`) and
the parent of an active sub-section. Any other element can opt in with
`data-scrollspy` around its own `a[href^="#"]` links — the DocsLayout
table of contents does. Without the script it is a plain list of links.

## Types

### `ScrollSpyItem`

One link of the spy; `href` is a hash to a section on the page.

| Prop | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string | Html` | yes |  |
| `href` | `string` | yes | `"#section-id"` — the element the link follows and the spy watches. |
| `children` | `ScrollSpyItem[]` |  | Sub-sections, drawn as a nested list. |

### `ScrollSpyProps`

| Prop | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `string` | yes |  |
| `items` | `ScrollSpyItem[]` | yes |  |
| `label` | `string` |  | The nav's accessible name. @default "On this page" |
| `offset` | `number` |  | Pixels under a sticky header where a section counts as "current". |
| `sticky` | `boolean` |  | Stick to the top of the viewport (under the sticky header) while its column scrolls. |
| `attrs` | `Attrs` |  |  |

## Usage

Each example as the rAPId call and the HTML it renders — the markup a plain page writes by hand. Icons are inline SVG in the real output; they are shortened to `<svg …>…</svg>` here.

### On this page, beside an article

Links to section ids; the section being read gets `aria-current` and `.is-active`, a sub-section marks its parent.

```ts
ScrollSpy({
  id: "guide-toc",
  items: [
    { label: "Overview", href: "#overview" },
    {
      label: "Install",
      href: "#install",
      children: [{ label: "Deno", href: "#install-deno" }, { label: "npm", href: "#install-npm" }],
    },
    { label: "Usage", href: "#usage" },
  ],
})
```

```html
<nav class="scrollspy" id="guide-toc" aria-label="On this page" data-scrollspy="">
  <ul class="scrollspy__list">
    <li class="scrollspy__item">
      <a class="scrollspy__link" href="#overview">Overview</a>
    </li>
    <li class="scrollspy__item">
      <a class="scrollspy__link" href="#install">Install</a>
      <ul class="scrollspy__list">
        <li class="scrollspy__item">
          <a class="scrollspy__link" href="#install-deno">Deno</a>
        </li>
        <li class="scrollspy__item">
          <a class="scrollspy__link" href="#install-npm">npm</a>
        </li>
      </ul>
    </li>
    <li class="scrollspy__item">
      <a class="scrollspy__link" href="#usage">Usage</a>
    </li>
  </ul>
</nav>
```

### Any list of hash links can be a spy

Add `data-scrollspy` to the element around the links — the DocsLayout table of contents is one.

```ts
html`
  <nav aria-label="Chapters" data-scrollspy data-scrollspy-offset="80">
    <a href="#one">One</a> <a href="#two">Two</a> <a href="#three">Three</a>
  </nav>
`
```

```html
<nav aria-label="Chapters" data-scrollspy data-scrollspy-offset="80">
  <a href="#one">One</a>
  <a href="#two">Two</a>
  <a href="#three">Three</a>
</nav>
```

## CSS hooks

Classes defined by `components/scrollspy/scrollspy.css` — structural, token-driven; override from an unlayered stylesheet (see [Theming](../UI-Theming.md)):

`.is-active`, `.scrollspy--sticky`, `.scrollspy__link`, `.scrollspy__list`

## Behaviour

`components/scrollspy/scrollspy.js` ships in `ui.js` (delegated on `document`, re-initialised after a rAPId swap).

Attributes it reads or writes: `data-scrollspy`, `data-scrollspy-offset`.

Events: `html:focus-within`, `rapid:swapped`.
